title: BEYOND STRUCTURE: INVARIANT CRYSTAL PROPERTY PREDICTION WITH PSEUDO-PARTICLE RAY DIFFRACTION
research_summary: Crystal property prediction, governed by quantum mechanical principles, is computationally prohibitive to solve exactly for large many-body systems using traditional density functional theory. While machine learning models have emerged as efficient approximations for large-scale applications, their performance is strongly influenced by the choice of atomic representation. Although modern graph-based approaches have progressively incorporated more structural information, they often fail to capture long-range atomic interactions due to finite receptive fields and local encoding schemes. This limitation leads to distinct crystals being mapped to identical representations, hindering accurate property prediction. To address this, we introduce PRDNet that leverages unique reciprocal-space diffraction besides graph representations. To enhance sensitivity to elemental and environmental variations, we employ a data-driven pseudo-particle to generate a synthetic diffraction pattern. PRDNet ensures full invariance to crystallographic symmetries. Extensive experiments are conducted on Materials Project, JARVIS-DFT, and MatBench, demonstrating that the proposed model achieves state-of-the-art performance.

title: A SINGLE ARCHITECTURE FOR REPRESENTING INVARIANCE UNDER ANY SPACE GROUP
research_summary: This paper introduces the Crystal Fourier Transformer (CFT), a single neural architecture that adapts its weights to enforce exact invariance to any input crystallographic space group. It achieves this by constructing symmetry-adapted Fourier bases through analytical derivation of constraints that group operations impose on Fourier coefficients, encoding these constraints into a group-conditional routing matrix (adjacency matrix of a dual graph). The architecture enables weight sharing across all 230 space groups, supports zero-shot generalization to unseen groups, and demonstrates competitive performance on material property prediction tasks.

title: Accurate prediction of tensorial spectra using equivariant graph neural network
research_summary: Here we introduce the Tensorial Spectra Equivariant Neural Network (TSENN), an equivariant graph neural network architecture that maps crystal structures directly to their full photon-frequency-dependent optical tensors. By encoding isotropic sequential scalar components and anisotropic sequential tensor components into spherical tensor representations, TSENN ensures symmetry-aware predictions consistent with crystalline symmetry constraints. Trained on frequency-dependent dielectric tensors of 1,432 bulk semiconductors, the model achieves a mean absolute error of 0.127, demonstrating its potential for efficient and general modeling of optical properties.

title: A framework to evaluate machine learning crystal stability predictions
research_summary: We present Matbench Discovery as an example evaluation framework for machine learning energy models, here applied as pre-filters to first-principles computed data in a high-throughput search for stable inorganic crystals.

title: Predicting thermodynamic stability of inorganic compounds using ensemble machine learning based on electron configuration
research_summary: This paper proposes an ensemble machine learning framework (ECSG) that integrates three base-level models—Magpie, Roost, and a newly developed Electron Configuration Convolutional Neural Network (ECCNN)—via stacked generalization to predict the thermodynamic stability of inorganic compounds. The method achieves high accuracy (AUC = 0.988 on JARVIS), exceptional sample efficiency (requiring only 1/7 the data of existing models), and strong generalization in unknown composition spaces (e.g., perovskite halides, Li-containing oxides, transition metal oxides). Validation includes computational (DFT) and experimental case studies on 2D wide bandgap semiconductors and double perovskite oxides.

title: Transformer-generated atomic embeddings to enhance prediction accuracy of crystal properties with machine learning
research_summary: This paper proposes a universal atomic embedding strategy called universal atomic embeddings (UAEs) generated by a home-made CrystalTransformer model, which learns unique 'fingerprints' for each atom capturing their roles and interactions within materials. The embeddings (ct-UAEs) are pre-trained on large crystal databases (MP*) for formation energy and bandgap prediction, then transferred to various back-end models (CGCNN, MEGNET, ALIGNN) to improve prediction accuracy across multiple datasets (MP, JARVIS, MC3D, hybrid perovskites). The work demonstrates improved MAE (e.g., 14% reduction for formation energy in CGCNN), transferability across tasks and databases, interpretability via clustering (UMAP/K-means revealing periodic-table-aligned groupings), and applicability to data-scarce domains like hybrid perovskites (34% MAE boost in MEGNET).

title: Accurate piezoelectric tensor prediction with equivariant attention tensor graph neural network
research_summary: The paper proposes an equivariant attention tensor graph neural network (EATGNN) to predict the full third-rank piezoelectric tensor for both bulk and 2D materials, leveraging irreducible representation decomposition to respect crystal symmetry and rotational equivariance. It validates predictions against DFT-calculated tensors, achieves state-of-the-art accuracy, and uses the model to screen and discover new high-performance piezoelectric candidates, subsequently confirmed by DFPT calculations.

title: Hierarchy-boosted funnel learning for identifying semiconductors with ultralow lattice thermal conductivity
research_summary: The paper proposes a hierarchy-boosted funnel learning (HiBoFL) framework that integrates unsupervised and supervised learning to efficiently identify semiconductors with ultralow lattice thermal conductivity (κL), circumventing large-scale brute-force ab initio calculations. It uses unsupervised clustering on a high-throughput dataset to narrow the search space, performs low-cost phonon-elasticity-thermal (PET) model-based high-throughput calculations on selected clusters to build a labeled local database, trains a CatBoost classifier to predict ultralow κL, and conducts interpretable SHAP analysis to uncover structural descriptors governing κL—especially discovering Lmin as a new factor influencing structural anharmonicity and phonon lifetime.

title: LLM-Prop: predicting the properties of crystalline materials using large language models
research_summary: This paper introduces LLM-Prop, a method that leverages large language models (LLMs) to predict properties of crystalline materials from their natural language text descriptions—generated by Robocrystallographer from CIF files—rather than from graph or structural representations. It proposes a fine-tuned T5 encoder architecture with specific preprocessing (e.g., [NUM]/[ANG] tokenization, [CLS] prepending, stopword removal) and label normalization strategies. The work benchmarks performance on six crystal properties (band gap, formation energy per atom, energy above hull, unit cell volume, energy per atom, direct/indirect band gap classification), demonstrates superiority over state-of-the-art GNNs and MatBERT, releases the TextEdge benchmark dataset, and analyzes ablation effects of design choices.

title: RETHINKING THE ROLE OF FRAMES FOR SE(3)-INVARIANT CRYSTAL STRUCTURE MODELING
research_summary: Crystal structure modeling with graph neural networks is essential for various applications in materials informatics, and capturing SE(3)-invariant geometric features is a fundamental requirement for these networks. A straightforward approach is to model with orientation-standardized structures through structure-aligned coordinate systems, or “frames.” However, unlike molecules, determining frames for crystal structures is challenging due to their infinite and highly symmetric nature. In particular, existing methods rely on a statically fixed frame for each structure, determined solely by its structural information, regardless of the task under consideration. Here, we rethink the role of frames, questioning whether such simplistic alignment with the structure is sufficient, and propose the concept of dynamic frames. While accommodating the infinite and symmetric nature of crystals, these frames provide each atom with a dynamic view of its local environment, focusing on actively interacting atoms. We demonstrate this concept by utilizing the attention mechanism in a recent transformer-based crystal encoder, resulting in a new architecture called CrystalFramer. Extensive experiments show that CrystalFramer outperforms conventional frames and existing crystal encoders in various crystal property prediction tasks.

title: A Denoising Pre-training Framework for Accelerating Novel Material Discovery
research_summary: The paper introduces an unsupervised Denoising Pre-training Framework (DPF) for crystal structures to overcome the scarcity of labeled data in crystal property prediction. DPF pre-trains models on 380,743 unlabeled crystal structures by reconstructing masked atom types, perturbed atom positions, and perturbed lattice constants; then fine-tunes the pre-trained models on downstream crystal property prediction tasks.

title: PDDFormer: Pairwise Distance Distribution Graph Transformer for Crystal Material Property Prediction
research_summary: The paper introduces WPDD (Atom-Weighted Pairwise Distance Distribution) and UPDD (Unit-cell Pairwise Distance Distribution) to construct continuous and geometrically complete multi-edge crystal graphs, integrating them into a transformer-based architecture (PDDFormer) for crystal material property prediction. It addresses discontinuity and incompleteness in prior crystal graph representations by modeling PDD as global information in matrix-based message passing, and validates continuity via Earth Mover’s Distance (EMD) and general geometric completeness via categorical induction. Experiments on Materials Project and JARVIS-DFT show state-of-the-art MAE across multiple properties including formation energy, band gap, bulk moduli, and shear moduli.

title: Accelerating materials property prediction via a hybrid Transformer Graph framework that leverages four body interactions
research_summary: We propose a framework utilizing a Graph Neural Network with composition-based and crystal structure-based architectures, combined with a transfer learning scheme. This approach accurately predicts energy-related properties (e.g., total energy, energy above the convex hull, energy band gap) and data-scarce mechanical properties (e.g., bulk and shear modulus). Our model incorporates four-body interactions, capturing periodicity and structural characteristics. It outperforms state-of-the-art models in 8 materials property regression tasks.

title: Cross-scale covariance for material property prediction
research_summary: A simulation can stand its ground against an experiment only if its prediction uncertainty is known. The unknown accuracy of interatomic potentials (IPs) is a major source of prediction uncertainty, severely limiting the use of large-scale classical atomistic simulations in a wide range of scientific and engineering applications. Here we explore covariance between predictions of metal plasticity, from 178 large-scale (~108 atoms) molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and a variety of indicator properties computed at small-scales (≤102 atoms). All simulations use the same 178 IPs. In a manner similar to statistical studies in public health, we analyze correlations of strength with indicators, identify the best predictor properties, and build a cross-scale “strength-on-predictors” regression model. This model is then used to estimate regression error over the statistical pool of IPs. Small-scale predictors found to be highly covariant with strength are computed using expensive quantum-accurate calculations and used to predict flow strength, within the statistical error bounds established in our study.

title: Advancing extrapolative predictions of material properties through learning to learn using extrapolative episodic training
research_summary: This study develops a meta-learning methodology—extrapolative episodic training (E2T)—to enhance the ability of machine learning models to predict material properties beyond the distribution of training data. Using attention-based matching neural networks (MNNs) trained on arbitrarily generated extrapolative episodes, the approach demonstrates superior generalization for unseen material domains in two case studies: predicting specific heat and refractive index of polymeric materials, and bandgap of hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites. The method enables rapid adaptation to target domains via fine-tuning with limited data.

title: Probing out-of-distribution generalization in machine learning for materials
research_summary: This paper systematically evaluates the out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization capabilities of various machine learning models across over 700 OOD tasks derived from three large ab initio materials databases (JARVIS, Materials Project, OQMD). It challenges the validity of heuristic-based OOD task definitions (e.g., leave-one-element-out, leave-one-space-group-out) by showing that most such tasks are not truly challenging—test data often reside within the representational domain of the training data (i.e., interpolation), not outside it (i.e., extrapolation). The study reveals that robust OOD performance is common even for simple models like XGBoost, and that neural scaling laws (improvement with larger training sets or longer training) fail for representationally OOD tasks, sometimes worsening performance. It introduces a representation-space-based method (using UMAP and kernel density estimation) to distinguish statistically OOD from representationally OOD test data, arguing that only the latter constitute genuinely challenging benchmarks.

title: Known Unknowns: Out-of-Distribution Property Prediction in Materials and Molecules
research_summary: Our objective is to train predictor models that extrapolate zero-shot to higher ranges than in the training data, given the chemical compositions of solids or molecular graphs and their property values. We propose using a transductive approach to OOD property prediction, achieving improvements in prediction accuracy. In particular, our method improves extrapolative precision by 1.8× for materials and 1.5× for molecules, and boosts recall of high-performing candidates by up to 3×. Our method leverages analogical input-target relations in the training and test sets, enabling generalization beyond the training target support, and can be applied to any other material and molecular tasks.

title: Dielectric tensor prediction for inorganic materials using latent information from preferred potential
research_summary: This study leverages multi-rank equivariant structural embeddings from a universal neural network potential to enhance predictions of dielectric tensors. We develop an equivariant readout decoder to predict total, electronic, and ionic dielectric tensors while preserving O(3) equivariance, and benchmark its performance against state-of-the-art algorithms. Virtual screening of thermodynamically stable materials from Materials Project for two discovery tasks, high-dielectric and highly anisotropic materials, identifies promising candidates including Cs2Ti(WO4)3 (band gap Eg = 2.93eV, dielectric constant ε = 180.90) and CsZrCuSe3 (anisotropic ratio αr = 121.89). The results demonstrate our model’s accuracy in predicting dielectric tensors and its potential for discovering novel dielectric materials.

title: A Space Group Symmetry Informed Network for O(3) Equivariant Crystal Tensor Prediction
research_summary: We consider the prediction of general tensor properties of crystalline materials, including dielectric, piezoelectric, and elastic tensors. A key challenge here is how to make the predictions satisfy the unique tensor equivariance to O(3) group and invariance to crystal space groups. To this end, we propose a General Materials Tensor Network (GMTNet), which is carefully designed to satisfy the required symmetries. To evaluate our method, we curate a dataset and establish evaluation metrics that are tailored to the intricacies of crystal tensor predictions. Experimental results show that our GMTNet not only achieves promising performance on crystal tensors of various orders but also generates predictions fully consistent with the intrinsic crystal symmetries.

title: COMPLETE AND EFFICIENT GRAPH TRANSFORMERS FOR CRYSTAL MATERIAL PROPERTY PREDICTION
research_summary: Crystal structures are characterized by atomic bases within a primitive unit cell that repeats along a regular lattice throughout 3D space. The periodic and infinite nature of crystals poses unique challenges for geometric graph representation learning. Specifically, constructing graphs that effectively capture the complete geometric information of crystals and handle chiral crystals remains an unsolved and challenging problem. In this paper, we introduce a novel approach that utilizes the periodic patterns of unit cells to establish the lattice-based representation for each atom, enabling efficient and expressive graph representations of crystals. Furthermore, we propose ComFormer, a SE(3) transformer designed specifically for crystalline materials. ComFormer includes two variants; namely, iComFormer that employs invariant geometric descriptors of Euclidean distances and angles, and eComFormer that utilizes equivariant vector representations. Experimental results demonstrate the state-of-the-art predictive accuracy of ComFormer variants on various tasks across three widely-used crystal benchmarks.

title: CRYSTALFORMER: INFINITELY CONNECTED ATTENTION FOR PERIODIC STRUCTURE ENCODING
research_summary: Predicting physical properties of materials from their crystal structures is a fundamental problem in materials science. In peripheral areas such as the prediction of molecular properties, fully connected attention networks have been shown to be successful. However, unlike these finite atom arrangements, crystal structures are infinitely repeating, periodic arrangements of atoms, whose fully connected attention results in infinitely connected attention. In this work, we show that this infinitely connected attention can lead to a computationally tractable formulation, interpreted as neural potential summation, that performs infinite interatomic potential summations in a deeply learned feature space. We then propose a simple yet effective Transformer-based encoder architecture for crystal structures called Crystalformer.

title: A Diffusion-Based Pre-training Framework for Crystal Property Prediction
research_summary: The paper proposes CrysDiff, a diffusion-based pretrain-finetune framework to address the challenge of crystal property prediction under sparse labeled data. It first pre-trains a model via self-supervised crystal structure reconstruction (learning p(F, L | A) from unlabeled 3D crystal structures), then fine-tunes it on limited labeled data to predict target properties (modeling p(y | A', F', L')). The method enforces crystal symmetries (O(3) invariance and periodic translation invariance) using an EGNN-based denoising model in both phases.

title: Structure-aware graph neural network based deep transfer learning framework for enhanced predictive analytics on diverse materials datasets
research_summary: This paper presents a structure-aware graph neural network (GNN) based deep transfer learning framework to improve predictive performance for materials properties using sparse data. It leverages the ALIGNN architecture trained on large source datasets (e.g., Materials Project formation energy) and applies transfer learning—via fine-tuning or feature extraction—to small target datasets across diverse materials classes (3D/2D, inorganic/organic, computational/experimental). The framework is evaluated on 115 dataset-property combinations, showing TL models outperform scratch-trained models in ≈90% of cases, especially for extrapolation and small-data regimes.

title: Higher-order equivariant neural networks for charge density prediction in materials
research_summary: We introduce ChargE3Net, an E(3)-equivariant graph neural network for predicting electron density in atomic systems. ChargE3Net enables the learning of higher-order equivariant features to achieve high predictive accuracy and model expressivity. We show that ChargE3Net exceeds the performance of prior work on diverse sets of molecules and materials. When trained on the massive dataset of over 100K materials in the Materials Project database, our model is able to capture the complexity and variability in the data, leading to a significant 26.7% reduction in self-consistent iterations when used to initialize DFT calculations on unseen materials. Furthermore, we show that non-self-consistent DFT calculations using our predicted charge densities yield near-DFT performance on electronic and thermodynamic property prediction at a fraction of the computational cost.

title: MD-HIT: Machine learning for material property prediction with dataset redundancy control
research_summary: This paper addresses the overestimation of machine learning model performance in materials science caused by dataset redundancy—i.e., highly similar materials in databases like Materials Project due to historical 'tinkering' in material design. It proposes MD-HIT, a redundancy reduction algorithm inspired by bioinformatics’ CD-HIT, with two variants: MD-HIT-composition (using composition-based distances like Mendeleev and MatScholar) and MD-HIT-structure (using structure-based distances like XRD and OFM). The authors apply MD-HIT to generate non-redundant datasets for formation energy and band gap prediction, then evaluate how redundancy control affects the predictive performance (R2, MAE) of state-of-the-art ML models (Roost, CrabNet, ALIGNN, DeeperGATGNN), demonstrating that reduced redundancy leads to lower—but more realistic—performance, especially for out-of-distribution (OOD) samples.

title: Virtual Node Graph Neural Network for Full Phonon Prediction
research_summary: The paper introduces the Virtual Node Graph Neural Network (VGNN) to predict phonon spectra and bandstructures directly from atomic coordinates, addressing challenges of variable-length output and complex unit cells. It presents three variants—vector (VVN), matrix (MVN), and momentum-dependent matrix (k-MVN) virtual nodes—to predict Γ-point phonons and full phonon dispersion. The method is validated on alloy systems and used to build a Γ-phonon database of over 146,000 materials from the Materials Project.

title: JARVIS-Leaderboard: a large scale benchmark of materials design methods
research_summary: JARVIS-Leaderboard is an open-source, community-driven platform for benchmarking and enhancing reproducibility in materials science. It integrates computational, experimental, and data-analytics methods across five categories—Artificial Intelligence (AI), Electronic Structure (ES), Force-fields (FF), Quantum Computation (QC), and Experiments (EXP)—and supports multiple data modalities (atomic structures, spectra, images, text). The platform hosts 274 benchmarks, 152 methods, 1281 contributions, and over 8 million data points, enabling systematic, transparent, and unbiased validation of materials design approaches.

title: Structure-based out-of-distribution (OOD) materials property prediction: a benchmark study
research_summary: This paper presents a comprehensive benchmark study evaluating graph neural network (GNN) models for predicting material properties on out-of-distribution (OOD) test sets—materials structurally or property-wise distinct from the training set. It introduces five OOD test set generation methods (LOCO, SparseXsingle, SparseXcluster, SparseYsingle, SparseYcluster) applied to three MatBench datasets (dielectric, elasticity, perovskites), trains and evaluates eight SOTA GNNs across 250 folds, and analyzes performance degradation relative to i.i.d. baselines, revealing significant generalization gaps and identifying CGCNN, ALIGNN, and DeeperGATGNN as comparatively robust.

title: A Recipe for Charge Density Prediction
research_summary: The paper proposes a machine learning method to predict the charge density of atomic systems—core quantum mechanical quantity from which all ground-state physicochemical properties derive—with both high accuracy and computational efficiency. It introduces three key ingredients: (1) representing charge density using atomic and virtual orbitals (spherical fields centered at atoms and bond midpoints), (2) using expressive, domain-informed, and learnable even-tempered Gaussian basis sets, and (3) employing a high-capacity SE(3)-equivariant neural network architecture (eSCN). The method achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on the QM9 charge density benchmark while being >30× faster than prior approaches, enabling flexible accuracy–efficiency trade-offs.

title: Learning Superconductivity from Ordered and Disordered Material Structures
research_summary: The paper introduces SuperCon3D, a new dataset containing both 3D crystal structures (ordered and disordered) and experimental superconducting transition temperatures (Tc), and proposes two deep learning models: SODNet for screening known structures to predict Tc, and DiffCSP-SC for generating novel high-Tc superconductor candidates. It validates the models by screening ICSD to identify candidate superconductors and generating novel structures, with some candidates further validated via DFT calculations for electronic features like Van Hove singularities.

title: How simple can you go? An off-the-shelf transformer approach to molecular dynamics
file_name: 32_How simple can you go - An off-the-shelf transformer approach to molecular dynamics.pdf
research_summary: This paper presents MD-ET, a minimally modified edge transformer architecture for molecular dynamics (MD) that intentionally omits built-in rotational equivariance and energy conservation—two common physical inductive biases in neural MD models. Trained on ∼30 × 106 structures from the QCML database via supervised pretraining, MD-ET achieves state-of-the-art results on multiple benchmarks after few-shot fine-tuning. The study evaluates how well an 'off-the-shelf' transformer can learn approximate equivariance and energy conservation purely from data, and assesses its ability to perform stable NVE and faithful NVT MD simulations.

title: Study on bandgap predications of ABX3-type perovskites by machine learning
file_name: 33_Study on bandgap predications of ABX3-type perovskites by machine learning.pdf
research_summary: The present work adopts machine learning (ML) to predict bandgaps of perovskites, where we collect 227 sets of experimental bandgap data of perovskites from the latest 1254 publications, to establish and identify 4 models from 24 kinds of ML models. The results of the models achieve high accuracy with root mean square error (RMSE) of down to 0.55 and meanwhile, the pearson correlation coefficient of up to 99%. In addition, our ML models give the effect of each chemical composition constituting the ABX3-type perovskites on the bandgaps by using the SHAP value, and they can be well explained in physics.

title: Physics-Informed Weakly Supervised Learning for Interatomic Potentials
file_name: 34_Physics-Informed Weakly Supervised Learning for Interatomic Potentials.pdf
research_summary: We address this challenge by introducing a physics-informed, weakly supervised approach for training machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs). We introduce two novel loss functions, extrapolating the potential energy via a Taylor expansion and using the concept of conservative forces. Our approach improves the accuracy of MLIPs applied to training tasks with sparse training data sets and reduces the need for pre-training computationally demanding models with large data sets.

title: Correcting DFT formation energies towards experimental accuracy using foundational MLIPs and latent-feature delta-learning
file_name: 35_Correcting DFT formation energies towards experimental accuracy using foundational MLIPs and latent-feature delta-learning.pdf
research_summary: The paper presents a two-stage correction framework to improve the agreement of density functional theory (DFT) formation energies with experimental values. First, it leverages foundational machine learning interatomic potentials (fMLIPs), specifically PET-OMATPES trained at the r2SCAN level, to compute zero-shot formation energies on DFT-relaxed geometries, reducing mean absolute error (MAE) by over 40% relative to GGA without additional DFT calculations. Second, it trains classical machine learning models (KRR, RF, GPR) in a delta-learning framework using the latent features of the fMLIP to predict the residual between the fMLIP-estimated formation energy and experiment, achieving a final MAE below 50 meV/atom—comparable to experimental uncertainty—while controlling the impact on relative phase stability through careful regularization.

title: Accelerating the Discovery of Hybrid Perovskites with Targeted Band Gaps via Interpretable Machine Learning
file_name: 36_Accelerating the Discovery of Hybrid Perovskites with Targeted Band Gaps via Interpretable Machine Learning.pdf
research_summary: This study combined feature engineering, the gradient-boosted regression tree (GBRT) algorithm, and the genetic algorithm-based symbolic regression (GASR) algorithm to develop an interpretable machine learning (ML) strategy for predicting the band gap of hybrid organic−inorganic perovskites (HOIPs) accurately and quantitatively interpreting the factors affecting the band gap. Seven best physical features were selected to construct a GBRT model with a root-mean-square error of less than 0.060 eV, and the most important feature is the electronegativity difference between the B-site and the X-site (χB−X). Further, a mathematical formula (Eg = χB−X^2 + 0.881χB−X) was constructed with GASR for a quantitative interpretation of the band gap influence patterns. According to the ML model, the HOIP MA0.23FA0.02Cs0.75Pb0.59Sn0.41Br0.24I2.76 was obtained, with a suitable band gap of 1.39 eV.

title: Assessing data-driven predictions of band gap and electrical conductivity for transparent conducting materials
file_name: 37_Assessing data-driven predictions of band gap and electrical conductivity for transparent conducting materials.pdf
research_summary: This paper proposes a data-driven framework to accelerate the discovery of new transparent conducting materials (TCMs) by creating and validating experimental databases of electrical conductivity and band gap, training state-of-the-art ML models on stoichiometry alone, and assessing their ability to identify previously unseen TCMs using a bespoke evaluation scheme—specifically, leave-one-TCM-family-out—on a list of 55 compositions.

title: Rational design of nanoscale stabilized oxide catalysts for OER with OC22
file_name: 38_Rational design of nanoscale stabilized oxide catalysts for OER with OC22.pdf
research_summary: This work uses pre-trained machine learning models from the Open Catalyst 2022 (OC22) framework to interpolate total energy predictions for OER surface intermediates on 4119 oxide materials, then constructs a flexible high-throughput screening framework to identify viable anode catalyst candidates for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) under bulk and nanoscale Pourbaix stability, material cost, overpotential, and metastability constraints.

title: A foundation machine learning potential with polarizable long-range interactions for materials modelling
file_name: 39_A foundation machine learning potential with polarizable long-range interactions for materials modelling.pdf
research_summary: We present a foundation framework that integrates explicit polarizable long-range physics with an equivariant graph neural network potential. It employs a physically motivated polarizable charge equilibration scheme that directly optimizes electrostatic interaction energies rather than partial charges. The foundation model, trained across the periodic table up to Pu, demonstrates strong performance across key materials modeling challenges. It effectively captures long-range interactions that are challenging for traditional message-passing mechanisms and accurately reproduces polarization effects under external electric fields. We have applied the model to mechanical properties, ionic diffusivity in solid-state electrolytes, ferroelectric phase transitions, and reactive dynamics at electrode-electrolyte interfaces, highlighting the model’s capacity to balance accuracy and computational efficiency. Furthermore, we show that as a foundation model, it can be efficiently finetuned to achieve high-level accuracy for specific challenging systems.

title: Atomic-scale revelation of in situ reverse regulation from particles to clusters in the Ni/La-CeOx catalyst
file_name: 40_Atomic-scale revelation of in situ reverse regulation from particles to clusters in the Ni-La-CeOx catalyst.pdf
research_summary: This work proposes and demonstrates a reverse regulation strategy—from metal particles to stable subnanometer clusters—enabled by rational design of catalytic environment and metal-support interaction, overcoming classical sintering limitations at high temperature. Using in situ characterization and theoretical calculations, it reveals atomic migration pathways and thermodynamic steady-state reconstruction underlying Ni cluster formation on La-doped CeO2 support during ammonia decomposition.

title: An efficient forgetting-aware fine-tuning framework for pretrained universal machine-learning interatomic potentials
file_name: 41_An efficient forgetting-aware fine-tuning framework for pretrained universal machine-learning interatomic potentials.pdf
research_summary: Pretrained universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) have revolutionized computational materials science by enabling rapid atomistic simulations as efficient alternatives to ab initio methods. Fine-tuning pretrained MLIPs offers a practical approach to improving accuracy for materials and properties where predictive performance is insufficient. However, this approach often induces catastrophic forgetting, undermining the generalizability that is a key advantage of pretrained MLIPs. Herein, we propose reEWC, an advanced fine-tuning strategy that integrates Experience Replay and Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC) to effectively balance forgetting prevention with fine-tuning efficiency. Using Li6PS5Cl (LPSC), a sulfide-based Li solid-state electrolyte, as a fine-tuning target, we show that reEWC significantly improves the accuracy of a pretrained MLIP, resolving well-known issues of potential energy surface softening and overestimated Li diffusivities. Moreover, reEWC preserves the generalizability of the pretrained MLIP and enables knowledge transfer to chemically distinct systems, including other sulfide, oxide, nitride, and halide electrolytes. Compared to Experience Replay and EWC used individually, reEWC delivers clear synergistic benefits, mitigating their respective limitations while maintaining computational efficiency. These results establish reEWC as a robust and effective solution for continual learning in MLIPs, enabling universal models that can advance materials research through large-scale, high-throughput simulations across diverse chemistries.

title: An open-access database and analysis tool for perovskite solar cells based on the FAIR data principles
file_name: 42_An open-access database and analysis tool for perovskite solar cells based on the FAIR data principles.pdf
research_summary: Here we extract all the meaningful device data from peer-reviewed papers on metal-halide perovskite solar cells published so far and make them available in a database. We collect data from over 42,400 photovoltaic devices with up to 100 parameters per device. We then develop open-source and accessible procedures to analyse the data, providing examples of insights that can be gleaned from the analysis of a large dataset. The database, graphics and analysis tools are made available to the community and will continue to evolve as an open-source initiative.

title: Machine learning for improved density functional theory thermodynamics
file_name: 43_Machine learning for improved density functional theory thermodynamics.pdf
research_summary: This work presents a machine learning approach to systematically correct intrinsic energy resolution errors in density functional theory (DFT) calculations of alloy formation enthalpies, improving reliability for ternary phase stability predictions. A neural network model is trained to predict the discrepancy (Hcorr = HDFT − Hexpt) between DFT-calculated and experimentally measured enthalpies of formation for binary and ternary alloys (specifically Al–Ni–Pd and Al–Ni–Ti), using structured features including elemental concentrations, atomic numbers, and interaction terms. The corrected enthalpies (Hpred = HDFT − Hcorr) enable more accurate determination of phase stability.

title: Precursor recommendation for inorganic synthesis by machine learning materials similarity from scientific literature
research_summary: This work uses a knowledge base of 29,900 solid-state synthesis recipes text-mined from the scientific literature to automatically learn which precursors to recommend for the synthesis of a novel target material. The approach learns chemical similarity of materials and refers the synthesis of a new target to precedent synthesis procedures of similar materials, mimicking human synthesis design. When proposing five precursor sets for each of 2,654 unseen test target materials, the recommendation strategy achieves a success rate of at least 82%.

title: Dataset of Solution-based Inorganic Materials Synthesis Recipes Extracted from the Scientific Literature
research_summary: This paper constructs a large-scale dataset of 35,675 solution-based inorganic materials synthesis 'recipes' extracted from scientific literature using advanced machine learning and natural language processing techniques. Each recipe contains precursors and target materials, their quantities, synthesis actions and attributes, and augmented reaction formulas. The work addresses the lack of large-scale databases for inorganic synthesis routes needed to enable data-driven approaches to AI-assisted synthesis design and optimization.

title: Atomistic Line Graph Neural Network for Improved Materials Property Predictions
research_summary: We develop Atomistic Line Graph Neural Network (ALIGNN) using a GNN architecture that performs message passing on both the interatomic bond graph and its line graph corresponding to bond angles. We demonstrate that angle information can be explicitly and efficiently included for materials to provide much improved performance. We train 44 models for predicting several solid-state material properties available in the JARVIS-DFT and materials-project databases. ALIGNN can outperform some of the previously known GNN models by up to 43.8 %.

title: PHYSICS GUIDED DEEP LEARNING FOR GENERATIVE DESIGN OF CRYSTAL MATERIALS WITH SYMMETRY CONSTRAINTS
research_summary: The paper proposes a Physics Guided Crystal Generative Model (PGCGM) for generative design of crystal materials with high structural diversity and symmetry, using deep learning integrated with physical constraints (atomic pairwise distance and structural symmetry) to improve generation validity and stability. Generated structures are validated via DFT calculations, with 1,869 out of 2,000 successfully optimized and deposited into the Carolina Materials Database; 39.6% have negative formation energy and 5.3% have energy-above-hull < 0.25 eV/atom.

title: The ab initio non-crystalline structure database: empowering machine learning to decode diffusivity
file_name: 507_The ab initio non-crystalline structure database_ empowering machine learning to decode diffusivity.pdf
research_summary: This paper presents the largest computed non-crystalline structure database to date, generated from systematic and accurate ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) calculations, covering 4849 compositions and 79 elements. It demonstrates how the database enables simple machine-learning models to predict Li-ion diffusivity with speed and accuracy as a cost-effective alternative to expensive DFT calculations. The work also explores using universal machine learning potentials (M3GNet, CHGNet) as surrogates for AIMD to accelerate non-crystalline structure generation.

title: Large Scale Benchmark of Materials Design Methods
research_summary: This work introduces JARVIS-Leaderboard, an open-source and community-driven platform that facilitates benchmarking and enhances reproducibility for materials design methods. The platform covers five categories: Artificial Intelligence (AI), Electronic Structure (ES), Force-fields (FF), Quantum Computation (QC), and Experiments (EXP), with benchmarks spanning atomic structures, spectra, images, and text. It includes 1281 contributions to 274 benchmarks using 152 methods and over 8 million data-points, enabling systematic, reproducible, transparent, and unbiased scientific development.

title: MatterChat: A Multi-Modal LLM for Material Science
research_summary: This paper introduces MatterChat, a multi-modal large language model that integrates atomic-level material structural data (via graph embeddings from CHGNet) with natural language prompts to enable human-AI interaction for material property prediction, structural analysis, and scientific reasoning. It uses a trainable bridge model to align frozen pretrained uMLIP (CHGNet) and LLM (Mistral-7B) components, enabling tasks such as chemical formula identification, space group classification, stability assessment, formation energy prediction, and step-by-step synthesis guidance — outperforming both general-purpose LLMs and physical ML models.

title: 1.5 million materials narratives generated by chatbots
research_summary: This paper addresses the bias in large language models (LLMs) toward 'hot' materials frequently found in scientific literature, which limits discovery of less-studied but potentially promising materials. To counteract this, the authors generate 1,494,017 natural language narratives describing materials drawn from ab initio databases (OQMD, Materials Project, JARVIS, COD, AFLOW2), aiming to produce a more balanced, periodic-table-even corpus for training specialized LLMs. Narratives are generated via a two-stage prompting pipeline using ChatGPT-3.5-turbo: first converting structured property data into descriptive text, then refining it into application-oriented explanations. The outputs are validated by human experts and GPT-4 across technical accuracy, language/structure, and relevance/depth.

title: An open benchmark for machine learning-based polymer property prediction
research_summary: The paper introduces Polymer Benchmark 2026 (PolyBench26), an open dataset of ~250,000 polymer-property datapoints across eight physical properties and four polymer architectures (homopolymers, alternating/random/block copolymers), sourced from experimental measurements, DFT, and MD simulations. It defines and executes four standardized evaluation tasks — in-distribution prediction, dataset-size scaling, repeat-unit complexity, and transfer to held-out architectures — to systematically compare language model, graph-based, and descriptor-based ML approaches for polymer property prediction. Graph-based models (PC, PPG) consistently outperform others across tasks.

title: Open Materials 2024 (OMat24) Inorganic Materials Dataset and Models
file_name: 516_Open Materials 2024 (OMat24) Inorganic Materials Dataset and Models.pdf
research_summary: The discovery and simulation of inorganic materials is core to diverse applications from climate change to semiconductor manufacturing. Artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to dramatically accelerate materials simulation, discovery and design. Although considerable progress has been made in developing training datasets and machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) architectures, the state-of-the-art in openly available and reproducible datasets and models lagged behind proprietary models. To address this issue, we present the Open Materials 2024 (OMat24) dataset, comprising over 110M DFT calculations across diverse chemistries, materials, and configurations. MLIP models trained on OMat24 achieve leading performance on the Matbench Discovery leaderboard, surpassing previous models with F1 scores above 0.9 for stability and 20 meV/atom accuracy for formation energy. Models trained on OMat24 also exhibit the highest accuracy in newly developed thermal conductivity and phonon prediction task benchmarks. We show that OMat24’s diversity corrects the consistent softening bias of prior models trained on less diverse datasets, which systematically underpredicted energy, forces, and derivative properties like phonons. The OMat24 dataset has allowed the research community to develop better model architectures, resulting in a step-change improvement inorganic material property prediction accuracy.

title: MACE: Higher Order Equivariant Message Passing Neural Networks for Fast and Accurate Force Fields
research_summary: Creating fast and accurate force fields is a long-standing challenge in computational chemistry and materials science. Recently, several equivariant message passing neural networks (MPNNs) have been shown to outperform models built using other approaches in terms of accuracy. However, most MPNNs suffer from high computational cost and poor scalability. We propose that these limitations arise because MPNNs only pass two-body messages leading to a direct relationship between the number of layers and the expressivity of the network. In this work, we introduce MACE, a new equivariant MPNN model that uses higher body order messages. In particular, we show that using four-body messages reduces the required number of message passing iterations to just two, resulting in a fast and highly parallelizable model, reaching or exceeding state-of-the-art accuracy on the rMD17, 3BPA, and AcAc benchmark tasks. We also demonstrate that using higher order messages leads to an improved steepness of the learning curves.

title: A Materials Map Integrating Experimental and Computational Data via Graph-Based Machine Learning for Enhanced Materials Discovery
research_summary: This study constructs interpretable materials maps that visualize relationships between structural features and experimental thermoelectric properties (zT), using an integrated dataset of computational structures and predicted experimental zT values. The maps are generated via graph-based deep learning (specifically MPNN within MatDeepLearn) followed by t-SNE dimensionality reduction, and are evaluated for structural organization (via nearest neighbor distance analysis) and interpretability — not for predictive accuracy. The work emphasizes supporting experimentalists in navigating synthesis-feasible regions of materials space based on structural similarity.

title: The NOMAD Artificial-Intelligence Toolkit: turning materials-science data into knowledge and understanding
research_summary: This paper introduces the NOMAD Artificial-Intelligence Toolkit, a web-browser-based infrastructure for interactive AI-based analysis of FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) materials-science data stored in the NOMAD Archive. It enables users to query, analyze, and model materials data via Jupyter notebooks, supporting reproducible, educational, and community-driven AI workflows — including exploratory clustering and predictive modeling (e.g., topological insulator classification) — without local software installation.

title: Latent Diffusion Pretraining for Crystal Property Prediction
research_summary: Fast and accurate prediction of crystal properties is a central challenge in new materials design. Graph neural networks and Transformer-based models have emerged as powerful tools for this task due to their ability to encode the local structural environment of atoms within a crystal. However, these models are data-hungry and in practice labeled data for crystal properties are very scarce. Pretraining–finetuning strategies, particularly those based on diffusion models, have shown promise in addressing these limitations. In this work, we introduce a novel latent-diffusion based pretraining framework CrysLDNet, designed to mitigate the data scarcity. Our approach integrates a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) with a diffusion model during the pretraining stage. The VAE encoder maps 3D crystal structures into a smooth latent space, within which the diffusion process is applied. This latent diffusion pretraining enables the graph encoder to effectively capture structural and chemical semantics from large-scale unlabeled data, which can then be finetuned for specific property prediction tasks.

title: Leveraging large language models to address data scarcity in machine learning for graphene synthesis
research_summary: This paper proposes LLM-based data imputation and feature engineering methods to enhance machine learning performance on scarce, heterogeneous datasets, demonstrated on graphene CVD synthesis data and the ML-HydPARK hydrogen storage dataset. GPT models perform data imputation via tailored prompting and semantic normalization of inconsistently reported features (e.g., CVD substrates). The methods markedly improve downstream performance: in graphene layer number classification using SVM, binary accuracy increases from 39% to 65% and ternary from 52% to 72%. Fine-tuning experiments show combining LLM-based data imputation and feature encoding with numerical ML predictors outperforms standalone fine-tuned LLM predictors in data-scarce settings.

title: CHIPS-FF: Evaluating Universal Machine Learning Force Fields for Material Properties
research_summary: We introduce CHIPS-FF (Computational High-Performance Infrastructure for Predictive Simulation-based Force Fields), an open-source benchmarking platform for machine learning force fields (MLFFs). This platform focuses on complex properties including elastic constants, phonon spectra, defect formation energies, surface energies, and interfacial and amorphous phase properties. Utilizing 16 graph-based MLFFs including ALIGNN-FF, CHGNet, MatGL, MACE, SevenNet, ORB, MatterSim, and OMat24, CHIPS-FF integrates the Atomic Simulation Environment (ASE) with JARVIS-Tools to facilitate high-throughput simulations. Our framework is tested on a set of 104 materials, including metals, semiconductors, and insulators representative of those used in semiconductor components, with each MLFF evaluated for convergence, accuracy, and computational cost. Additionally, we evaluate the force-prediction accuracy of these models for close to 2 million atomic structures. By offering a streamlined, flexible benchmarking infrastructure, CHIPS-FF aims to guide the development and deployment of MLFFs for real-world semiconductor applications, bridging the gap between quantum mechanical simulations and large-scale device modeling.

title: MaterialsGalaxy: A Platform Fusing Experimental and Theoretical Data in Condensed Matter Physics
research_summary: MaterialsGalaxy is a platform that deeply fuses heterogeneous experimental and theoretical data in condensed matter physics using a structure similarity-driven data fusion mechanism. It links cross-modal records (diffraction, crystal growth, computations, literature) based on atomic structures, integrates AI tools (LLMs, generative models, ML property predictors), and enables dynamic data augmentation via structural analogs to bridge experiment-theory gaps and accelerate materials discovery.

title: Graph Networks as a Universal Machine Learning Framework for Molecules and Crystals
research_summary: This paper develops universal MatErials Graph Network (MEGNet) models for accurate property prediction in both molecules and crystals, addressing limitations of prior ML models—including domain specificity (molecules vs. crystals), lack of global state handling (e.g., temperature), and data scarcity—through graph networks with global state attributes, unified free energy modeling, and transfer learning of elemental embeddings.

title: Insights into CO dimerization at electrified Cu interfaces from large-scale machine learning simulations
research_summary: The paper introduces the Open Catalyst 2025 (OC25) dataset—the largest solid–liquid interface dataset for electrocatalysis—and uses OC25-trained machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) to perform large-scale, explicit-solvent simulations of CO dimerization on Cu surfaces. It computes free-energy profiles under varied surface charge, cation identity, and surface facet (Cu(100) vs Cu(310)), revealing weak sensitivity to charge/cation except at highly negative potentials, and identifies stepped Cu(310) as a more favorable pathway with exergonic dimerization at modest reducing potentials.

title: Orb: A Fast, Scalable Neural Network Potential
research_summary: We introduce Orb, a family of universal interatomic potentials for atomistic modelling of materials. Orb models are 3-6 times faster than existing universal potentials, stable under simulation for a range of out of distribution materials and, upon release, represented a 31% reduction in error over other methods on the Matbench Discovery benchmark. We explore several aspects of foundation model development for materials, with a focus on diffusion pretraining. We evaluate Orb as a model for geometry optimization, Monte Carlo and molecular dynamics simulations.

title: Machine learning with force-field inspired descriptors for materials: fast screening and mapping energy landscape
research_summary: The paper introduces classical force-field inspired descriptors (CFID) — combining radial, nearest neighbor, bond-angle, dihedral-angle, and core-charge distributions with chemical descriptors — to enable accurate machine learning prediction of multiple material properties. Using gradient boosting decision trees trained on the JARVIS-DFT database (24,549 bulk + 616 monolayer materials), it achieves high accuracy for formation energies, bandgaps, refractive indices, magnetic properties, elastic moduli, and exfoliation energies. The models are applied to screen exfoliable 2D semiconductors and integrated with a genetic algorithm to map energy landscapes (convex hulls) for multicomponent systems, validating against DFT.

title: Five High-Impact Research Areas in Machine Learning for Materials Science
research_summary: This editorial outlines five high-impact research areas in materials informatics: (1) validation by experiment or physics-based simulation; (2) ML approaches tailored for materials data and applications; (3) high-throughput data acquisition capabilities; (4) ML that makes scientists more effective (e.g., explainability, accelerated characterization); and (5) integration of physics within ML and with physics-based simulations. It emphasizes challenges including sparse/noisy/heterogeneous data, need for validation beyond model fitting, uncertainty quantification, extrapolation detection, descriptor development, generative design, and physics-informed modeling.

title: AI-driven design of multiprincipal element alloys for optimal water splitting
research_summary: This paper develops an AI framework integrating Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) with a configuration entropy–based acquisition function and Design of Experiments (DoE) to screen and optimize multiprincipal element alloys (MPEAs) for water splitting electrocatalysis. Through Bayesian optimization across 16.2 million compositions, it identifies Fe12Co28Ni33Mo17Pd5Pt5 as the optimal composition, achieving ultralow overpotentials (24 mV for HER, 204 mV for OER at 10 mA·cm−2) and robust stability, surpassing state-of-the-art benchmarks.

title: Superconducting gap of H3S measured by tunnelling spectroscopy
research_summary: This paper characterizes the superconducting gap structure in the high-temperature superconductor H3S and its deuterium counterpart D3S using tunnelling spectroscopy measurements. The work provides direct experimental evidence for superconductivity from a microscopic perspective, validates the phonon-mediated pairing mechanism, and identifies multigap features in multiphase hydrogen sulfide samples.

title: Quadruple-band synglisis enables high thermoelectric efficiency in earth-abundant tin sulfide crystals
research_summary: We improved the thermoelectric efficiency in SnS crystals by promoting the convergence of energy and momentum of four valance bands, termed quadruple-band synglisis. We introduced more Sn vacancies to activate quadruple-band synglisis and facilitate carrier transport by inducing SnS2 in selenium (Se)–alloyed SnS, leading to a high dimensionless figure of merit (ZT) of ~1.0 at 300 kelvin and an average ZT of ~1.3 at 300 to 773 kelvin in p-type SnS crystals. We further obtained an experimental efficiency of ~6.5%, and our fabricated cooler demonstrated a maximum cooling temperature difference of ~48.4 kelvin at 353 kelvin.

title: Electrochemical metrics for corrosion resistant alloys
research_summary: This paper presents a curated database of electrochemical metrics for corrosion resistant alloys (CRAs), collected from 85 publications, to enable machine learning–based exploration of compositional space beyond existing empirical models. The database includes six categories of metrics: pitting potential (Epit), repassivation potential (Erp), crevice corrosion potential (Ecrev), pitting temperature (Tpit), crevice corrosion temperature (Tcrev), and corrosion potential (Ecorr), corrosion current density (icorr), passivation current density (ipass), and corrosion rate. It covers Al- and Fe-based alloys, high entropy alloys (HEAs), and Ni-Cr-Mo ternary systems, with associated experimental metadata (e.g., composition, temperature, chloride concentration, pH, test solution, microstructure). The dataset is intended to support the design and optimization of highly corrosion resistant alloys.

title: Additively-manufactured Al-0.3Zr-0.2Ce-0.2Cu alloy with high creep resistance and electrical conductivity
research_summary: A new, solute-lean Al-0.3Zr-0.2Ce-0.2Cu (wt.%) alloy is developed for additive manufacturing that overcomes the classical tradeoff between conductivity and creep resistance. The rapid-cooling-enabled supersaturation of Zr, and its uniform distribution in α-Al matrix, along with formation of submicron (Ce,Cu)-rich intermetallic particles on solidification lead to unusually high creep resistance at 200 oC. Near-zero secondary creep rates are achieved up to the alloy yield stress (YS) of 65 MPa at 200 °C in as-fabricated state. The Zr-solute-induced dislocation-climb suppression mechanism underlying this improvement also restricts dynamic recovery above YS, as noted from appreciable primary creep and its transitioning to near-zero secondary creep rates. A combination of relatively coarse, epitaxially-grown α-Al grains, low Zr concentration in α-Al, and the impurity-scavenging effect of Ce to purify α-Al matrix produces high electrical conductivity of ~48 %IACS. Aging precipitation of L12-Al3Zr nanoprecipitates doubles the YS (to ~150 MPa) at room temperature and increases alloy conductivity to ~58 %IACS, but loss of solid-solution Zr out of α-Al matrix leads to activation of dislocation climb, degrading the creep properties as compared to the supersaturated Al-Zr solid solution in the as-fabricated state. Compared to L12-Al3Zr nanoprecipitates, submicron (Ce,Cu)-rich particles formed on solidification are more effective at impeding dislocation climb, producing a threshold stress for dislocation creep of ~ 50 MPa at 200 °C. The new alloy design concepts, especially solute-induced dislocation-climb suppression for creep resistance, explored here may pave way for the design of new metallic alloys for thermal/electrical conductors and other high-temperature applications.

title: Compositional evolution of Q-phase precipitates in an aluminum alloy
research_summary: Here we employ a combination of atom-probe tomography (APT), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), transmission electron-microscopy, X-ray diffraction and first-principles calculations to reveal the compositional evolution of Q-phase precipitates in a commercial, age-hardenable aluminum alloy, W319. Three different aging conditions are investigated: 438 K/8 h, 463 K/8 h and 533 K/4 h. Co-precipitation of h'- and Q-phase precipitates is observed for all aging conditions, which, when combined with DSC analysis of the precipitation sequence, suggests that Q-phase precipitates serve as heterogeneous nucleation sites for h'-platelets. Regarding composition evolution, aging at the lower temperatures yields Q-phase precipitates that are Cu-rich, yet deficient in Mg and Si: 44Al–22Cu–16Mg–16.5Si at.%. The composition evolves to become Mg-rich after aging at 533 K: ~28Al–9Cu–37Mg–26Si at.%. APT provides evidence for partitioning of Zn to the Q-phase precipitates. The energetics of Zn partitioning was evaluated using first-principles calculations, and suggests that this partitioning is a kinetic effect.

title: Microstructure Evolution and Mechanical Properties of X6CrNiMoVNb11-2 Stainless Steel after Heat Treatment
research_summary: This paper investigates how quenching and tempering heat treatments affect the microstructure and mechanical properties of X6CrNiMoVNb11-2 supermartensitic stainless steel, with the goal of optimizing process parameters (e.g., quenching at 1040 °C in oil, tempering at 650 °C in air) to achieve target hardness (~313 HV), elongation (17.9%), reduction of area (52%), and impact toughness (~65 J/cm2). It analyzes phase transformations (Ms, Mf, Ac1, Ac3), nanophase precipitation (M23C6, Ni3Mo, Ni3Nb), and derives a tempered hardness equation.

title: Molecular structural dataset of lignin macromolecule elucidating experimental structural compositions
research_summary: The paper presents the Lignin Structural (LGS) Dataset, which includes 60 K computer-generated molecular structures of milled wood lignin focusing on coniferyl and syringyl monomeric units and six common interunit linkages. Structural data were generated using a sequence-controlled polymer generation approach calibrated to match experimental lignin properties, covering polymer chains of length 3–25 monomer units. The dataset matches experimental structural compositions with ~90% accuracy and serves as a resource for computational simulation and predictive modelling of lignin.

title: Quantitative Structure−Permittivity Relationship Study of a Series of Polymers
research_summary: This paper develops quantitative structure–property relationship (QSPR) models to predict the dielectric constant (ε) of polymers using machine learning, specifically a genetic algorithm combined with multiple linear regression (GA-MLRA). It uses structural descriptors computed from monomer units of 71 diverse polymers, validates models via internal and external validation (including test set, LOO cross-validation, y-scrambling, and Williams plots), and proposes two mechanistically explainable models (4- and 8-descriptor) with high predictive performance (R2_train = 0.905, R2_test = 0.812 for the best model).

title: Measuring the onset of sintering using laser ultrasonics
file_name: 211_Journal of the American Ceramic Society - 2025 - Nissen - Measurcs.pdf
research_summary: A noncontact laser ultrasonics method for determining the onset temperature and the early stage sintering state is studied. Because this technique measures properties near the surface in selected regions on the sample, it is particularly well-suited to parts produced by additive manufacturing routes such as selective laser flash sintering, where local variations in sintering state along one dimension result from the laser scan pattern. We demonstrate the ability to measure very small changes in interparticle neck size by measuring Rayleigh wave speeds. The changes in wave speed result initially from rapid changes in Young’s modulus that occur at the onset and in the early stages of sintering, before significant densification is observed. This measurement method is demonstrated using alumina pellets that were partially sintered at different temperatures to produce parts with a range of neck sizes and relative densities. Using the laser ultrasonics technique, the onset of sintering is detected at temperatures between 520◦C and 650◦C, which is significantly below the onset sintering temperatures detectable using traditional methods.

title: Porosity dependence of sound velocities in partially sintered alumina, zirconia, ATZ, and mullite ceramics
file_name: 212_ndence of sound velocities in partially sintered.pdf
research_summary: This paper experimentally measures and compares sound velocities (longitudinal and transverse) and Young’s modulus in partially sintered alumina, zirconia, ATZ composite, and mullite ceramics across a broad porosity range, then evaluates how well various theoretical models—such as exponential, percolation, differential, self-consistent, and numerical benchmark relations—predict the observed porosity dependence.

title: Low-Temperature Densification of Si3N4 Ceramics With MnO as a Sintering Additive
research_summary: Dense Si3N4 ceramics were fabricated by spark plasma sintering (SPS) using a MnO–Al2O3 additive system, and the effects of sintering temperature, pressure and holding time on densification behavior, phase transformation, microstructure development and mechanical properties were systematically investigated. Near-theoretical densification was achieved at a relatively low temperature of 1450◦C, demonstrating the strong fluxing effect of MnO in promoting liquid-phase-assisted sintering. The α–β phase transformation was found to be highly sensitive to the sintering conditions, enabling continuous tuning of the α/β phase ratio over a wide range. This controlled phase transformation resulted in pronounced microstructural changes, from fine equiaxed α-Si3N4 grains to elongated columnar β-Si3N4 grains, leading to a broad and tunable hardness-fracture toughness range.

title: Constructing high-polarization silica for polyimide-based nanocomposites with enhanced dielectric permittivity and mechanical performances: Molecular dynamics simulations
research_summary: This work employs silane coupling agents with different functional groups (PhCOOH, NH2, Ph, PhNH2, PhCOCH3) to modify the interfaces of polyimide/SiO2 (PIS) nanocomposites, and predicts the effects of interfacial structures on dielectric and mechanical properties using molecular dynamics simulation. The results show that the PhCOOH-modified interface simultaneously elevates static dielectric permittivity (εs) and Young modulus due to enhanced intrinsic polarization of SiO2 particles, interface polarization, increased hydrogen bonds, non-bond interactions, and improved interfacial load transfer efficiency.

title: A dataset of micro-scale tomograms of unidirectional glass fibre/epoxy and carbon fibre/epoxy composites acquired via synchrotron computed tomography during in-situ tensile loading
research_summary: This paper presents a publicly available dataset of 3D synchrotron X-ray computed tomography (XCT) images of two unidirectional fiber-reinforced composites — glass/epoxy and carbon/epoxy — acquired during in-situ tensile loading at four load levels (0%, 40%, 73%, and 95% of failure load). The data consists of raw and filtered (non-local means + ring artifact removal) 8-bit TIFF image stacks, cropped to volumes of interest (VOIs) from the middle 0° plies, enabling microstructural analysis of fiber distribution, orientation, misalignment, and break formation under load.

title: Pt Single Atom Co-Catalysts on Thin, Defined Anatase Layers: Critical Factors for Photocatalytic Hydrogen Generation
research_summary: This study systematically investigates platinum single atoms deposited on anatase TiO2 thin films grown on fluorine-doped tin oxide with defined thickness and crystallographic structure, by direct-current sputter-deposition of titania. Comprehensive parameter screening shows that variations in Pt precursor concentration, pre-annealing temperature, and TiO2 layer thickness significantly influence the photocatalytic performance. Crucially, a Langmuir-type adsorption behavior for Pt single atoms is demonstrated and extract an optimal surface density of ≈4 × 105 SAs μm−2 (around 0.26 at.% Pt) – higher loading does not further enhance photocatalytic activity. For optimized co-catalyst loading, variations in TiO2 thickness and structure remain the primary factors influencing photocatalytic performance through charge transport, and light absorption as key parameters. This optimal loading is confined to the surface of the TiO2 film and is sufficient to fully utilize the photogenerated electron flux under ultravoilet excitation. This work introduces the concept of a critical co-catalyst density that separates the transition from co-catalyst-limited to absorber-limited behavior in SAC-based photocatalysis, thereby contributing to a further rational design of photocatalytic systems.

title: Optimizing the thermoelectric performance of n-type PbSe through dynamic doping driven by entropy engineering
research_summary: This work synthesizes a series of entropy-increased n-type lead chalcogenide compounds Pb1−ySnySe1−xTexSx-2at%Cu to optimize the thermoelectric performance of n-type PbSe via dynamic doping driven by entropy engineering. The strategy combines configurational entropy enhancement (via Te/S/Sn alloying) with Cu interstitial doping to simultaneously improve Seebeck coefficient and reduce lattice thermal conductivity, achieving a peak ZT of ~1.46 at 623 K and record room-temperature ZT of ~0.64 for n-type PbSe.

title: Effect of Fiber–Matrix Interface Friction on Compressive Strength of High-Modulus Carbon Composites
research_summary: This work investigates why intermediate-modulus (IM) carbon fibers exhibit stronger fiber–matrix interface strength than high-modulus (HM) carbon fibers in hybrid carbon-fiber-reinforced polymer (CFRP) composites, focusing on the role of interface friction arising from surface topology differences. Using SEM imaging and in situ SEM-based push-out and push-back experiments, the authors measure and compare interface shear strength (IFSS) and interface friction strength for IM and HM fibers in a nanosilica-toughened hybrid CFRP, revealing ~48% higher interface friction for IM fibers—attributed to their rougher, grooved surface versus the smoother HM fiber surface—and linking this difference to improved compressive strength.

title: Enhanced Toughness in Amide Group-Modified Polyethylene Through N−H···O Hydrogen Bond Dissociation
research_summary: This study employs molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and density functional theory (DFT) calculations to investigate how different functional groups (keto, ester, amide) modulate the structural and mechanical behavior of polyethylene at the atomic scale, with a focus on elucidating the microscopic mechanisms behind enhanced toughness and tensile strength in amide-functionalized PE (AMPE) via N−H···O hydrogen bond dissociation.

title: A Bifunctional Aminoxyl−Bipyridine Peptide Catalyst for the Atroposelective Copper-Catalyzed Aerobic Oxidation of Biaryl Diols
research_summary: This paper reports the design, synthesis, and application of a novel bifunctional chiral peptide catalyst containing both an aminoxyl and a bipyridyl motif (Aminoxyl−Peptide−BpyAla) for the atroposelective copper(I)-catalyzed aerobic oxidation of prochiral biaryl diols to yield axially chiral monoaldehydes with high enantiomeric ratios (up to >99.5:0.5 er). The work demonstrates that bifunctionality—co-localization of both catalytic motifs within a single peptide scaffold—is essential for enantioselectivity, as monofunctional analogues (aminoxyl-only or bipyridyl-only peptides) gave racemic products. Mechanistic studies (kinetics, DFT modeling) support a monomeric active catalyst species with a rigid, sterically confined chiral environment around copper, where selectivity arises from a combination of enantiotopic group selection and secondary kinetic resolution.

title: Large plasticity in magnesium mediated by pyramidal dislocations
research_summary: The paper investigates the fundamental deformation mechanism responsible for large plasticity in submicrometer-size magnesium single crystals, specifically resolving the controversy around the mobility and slip planes of ⟨c+a⟩ dislocations under c-axis compression at room temperature. Using in situ TEM mechanical testing, 3D tomography, and atomistic simulations, the authors demonstrate that ⟨c+a⟩ dislocations are glissile and accommodate plastic strain by gliding on both pyramidal I {101̄1} and pyramidal II {112̄2} planes, including cross-slip between them, thereby explaining the observed high strength and ductility.

title: Long-Term Creep-Rupture Behavior of Alloy Inconel 740/740H
research_summary: This manuscript analyzes an extensive creep-rupture dataset for Ni-based superalloy Inconel 740/740H (650–875°C, up to ~70,000 h) using Larson-Miller parameter (LMP) and Wilshire analytical approaches to assess their effectiveness in describing experimental data and—critically—in predicting long-term creep-limited lifetimes (e.g., ≥100,000 h) from shorter-term data (<5,000 h). The study evaluates prediction accuracy by direct comparison of model-predicted rupture times against measured values, identifies mathematical instability ('turnback') in the LMP formalism under extrapolation, and concludes the Wilshire approach is superior for long-term lifetime forecasting.

title: Experiment and Modelling of the Pre-Strain Effect on the Creep Behaviour of P/M Ni-Based Superalloy FGH96
research_summary: This study investigates how room-temperature pre-strain affects the high-temperature creep behaviour of P/M Ni-based superalloy FGH96, combining experimental creep testing (at 700 °C and 690 MPa) with microstructural characterization (OM, SEM, TEM) and development of a physics-based steady-state creep rate model that explicitly incorporates the micro-twinning mechanism and pre-strain-induced mobile dislocation density evolution.

title: Effect of chromium-to-carbon ratio and carbide volume fraction on the three-body abrasion wear and corrosion behaviour of high chromium white cast iron
research_summary: A systematic compositional matrix of twelve as-cast alloys (13.2–30.8 wt% Cr; 1.95–3.96 wt% C) was designed to elucidate the combined influence of chromium-to-carbon ratio (Cr/C = 4.19–15.32) and carbide volume fraction (22.5–44.2%) on microstructure and multi-property response. Thermodynamic modelling integrated with real-time thermal analysis shows that non-equilibrium solidification underpins matrix constitution and carbide evolution, with pronounced deviations from equilibrium predictions. X-ray diffraction and microscopy confirm M7C3 as the dominant carbide with a Cr/C-dependent transition between austenitic and martensitic matrices driven by chromium partitioning. Mechanical and tribological properties showed pronounced non-linearity, with an optimal compositional window (Cr/C = ~12; CVF = ~33%) maximising hardness, fracture toughness and three-body abrasion resistance. Corrosion resistance correlates mainly with matrix chromium availability, revealing a trade-off between wear and electrochemical performance. The results establish Cr/C ratio and carbide fraction as predictive design variables for engineering optimisation of as-cast HCWCIs in demanding service environments.

title: Effect of cryogenic treatment on microstructural evolution and impact abrasive wear performance of Cr26 high-chromium cast iron
research_summary: This work adopted a combined heat treatment strategy to tailor the microstructural features of martensite, retained austenite, and secondary carbides in high-chromium cast iron, and systematically examined their influences on mechanical properties and impact abrasive wear behavior.

title: Effect of Sintering Parameters on the Densification, Microstructure, and Mechanical Performance of ZrB2–SiC Ceramics
file_name: 235_Int J Applied Cemeters on the Densification  Microstructure  and.pdf
research_summary: This study systematically investigates the independent and combined effects of three critical spark plasma sintering (SPS) parameters—temperature, applied pressure, and dwell time—on the densification behavior, microstructure, and mechanical properties of ZrB2–20 vol% SiC composites. It evaluates two powder preparation routes (WC-milled vs. ZrO2-milled) to assess how sintering parameter sensitivity depends on processing history and impurity levels, aiming to optimize additive-free, energy-efficient processing for aerospace and thermal protection applications.

title: Postsynthetic modification of yttria-stabilized zirconia aerogels with silica coatings for enhanced thermal stability
file_name: 236_Journal of the American Ceramic Society - 2024 - Olson - Postsynthetic modification of yttria‐stabilized zirconia aerogels.pdf
research_summary: The current work aims to improve the pore structure stability of yttria-stabilized zirconia aerogels by the addition of a SiO2 coating. The functionalization of surface hydroxyl groups by the addition of SiO2 is hypothesized to mitigate condensation reactions, which are a driving force for shrinkage and pore structure collapse. Zirconia aerogels with 0, 10, and 30 mol% yttria (YO1.5) additions were coated in a tetraethyl orthosilicate (TEOS) solution and exposed to temperatures up to 1200◦C. Crystal structure, pore structure, and aerogel morphology were investigated to understand changes in aerogel thermal stability. The SiO2 coating exhibited a greater influence on pore stability over yttria concentration, with specific surface area of the coated aerogels being twice that of the uncoated aerogels up to 1000◦C. However, the presence of the SiO2 coating promoted rapid sintering and densification at 1200◦C, establishing an upper use temperature for SiO2 and a need to develop other coating chemistries.

title: Nitrogen Interstitial Alloying of CoCrFeMnNi High Entropy Alloy through Reactive Powder Milling
research_summary: The present work is focused on the synthesis of CoCrFeMnNi high entropy alloy (HEA) interstitially alloyed with nitrogen via powder metallurgy routes. Using a simple method, nitrogen was introduced to the HEA from the protective N2 gas atmosphere during mechanical alloying (MA) processing. The lattice parameter and amount of nitrogen in HEA were observed to be linearly proportional to the milling duration. The limited solubility of nitrogen in the main face centered cubic (FCC) phase resulted in the in-situ formation of nitrides and, accordingly, significant increase in the hardness values. It has been shown that fabrication of such nitrogen-doped HEA bulk materials can be conveniently achieved by a simple combination of MA + spark plasma sintering processes, without the need for adding nitrogen from other sources.
