title: A Study on the Susceptibility to SCC of 7050 Aluminum Alloy by DCB Specimens
research_summary: The stress corrosion cracking (SCC) of different aging states for 7050 aluminum alloy in 3.5% sodium chloride aqueous solution has been studied by means of double cantilever beam (DCB) specimens, cathodic polarization, scanning electron microscope (SEM), transmission electron microscope (TEM) and time-of-flying second ion mass spectrometer (ToF-SIMS). The results showed that the susceptibility to SCC (Iscc) of 7050 aluminum alloy decreases with increasing the aging time. When a cathodic polarization potential of −1100 mV was applied to DCB specimens, the ion current intensity of hydrogen (IH+) near the crack tip and Iscc increased obviously, thus the degree of the diffusion of hydrogen into the grain boundary become more serious. The observation of microstructure indicated that the precipitates on the grain boundary become coarse and are sparsely distributed with increasing the aging time of 7050 aluminum alloy.

title: Pressure filtration and sintering of ultra-high-density Al2O3 green bodies
research_summary: A high-density green body is critical for producing fine-grained ceramics at low sintering temperatures. However, achieving high density from submicron powders is challenging due to their high specific surface area. In this study, an alumina slurry using a super-fine α-Al2O3 powder (d50 = 180 nm) and a low molecular weight dispersant (CE-64) was prepared with a high solid loading of 55 vol% and a low viscosity of 0.40 Pa⋅s. The slurry was post-treated by pressure filtration at 0.4 MPa. After de-binding at 750◦C, the resulting green bodies exhibited a relative density of 67.4%, 0.9% higher than that of the counterparts formed without pressure filtration. Pressureless sintering at 1300◦C in air yielded ceramics with a relative density of 99.97%, an average grain size of 0.70 μm, a flexural strength of 631 MPa, and a hardness of 18.5 GPa. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of achieving high-performance alumina ceramics with fine-grained microstructures under simplified sintering conditions through the combined use of high solid loading slurry and low-pressure filtration forming.

title: Effect of Cross-Link Homogeneity on the High-Strain Behavior of Elastic Polymer Networks
research_summary: This paper investigates how cross-link homogeneity (random vs. regular network architecture) affects the high-strain mechanical behavior—specifically the onset of strain stiffening—of poly(n-butyl acrylate) networks, using a double-network strategy to overcome premature fracture. It synthesizes and compares randomly cross-linked networks (via free-radical polymerization) and regularly cross-linked networks (via thiol-bromine click coupling of tetrafunctional star polymers), then swells both in monomer/cross-linker and polymerizes to form double networks for uniaxial tensile testing. Results show that, for networks with the same modulus, regular networks exhibit delayed strain stiffening relative to random ones, indicating that low- and high-strain responses arise from distinct molecular-scale features (defect content vs. elastically effective strand length).

title: Synergetic Improvement of Interfacial Performance and Impact Resistance of Carbon Fiber-Reinforced Epoxy Composite via Continuous Electrochemical Oxidation
research_summary: This study elucidated the synergistic improvement of the interfacial performance and impact resistance of carbon fiber-reinforced epoxy (CF/EP) composites by employing continuous electrochemical oxidation. CFs were electrochemically treated at different current densities, and the surface physicochemical properties, including the surface morphologies, chemical compositions, and wettabilities, were analyzed. After electrochemical oxidation, the IFSS of the CF/EP increased by 48.8%, significantly improving the impact resistance of the composites. The experimental results showed that, when the current density reached 0.15 mA/cm2, the damage area after impact reduced by 61%. Concurrently, fiber fracture and resin failure became the primary energy-dissipation modes, maximizing the fiber reinforcement effect and enhancing the impact resistance. However, fiber fracture deteriorated the static mechanical properties of the composites. Subsequently, at a 0.10 mA/cm2 current density, the CF/EP composites exhibited an increased compressive strength after an impact of 331 MPa.

title: Unexpected field evaporation sequence in γ-TiAl: Interpreting field evaporation through dynamic bond-breaking processes
research_summary: This paper investigates the counterintuitive field evaporation sequence in [001]-oriented γ-TiAl using full-dynamics molecular dynamics simulations (TAPSim-MD), revealing that Ti atoms evaporate preferentially over Al despite stronger Ti–Ti bonds, due to a two-step bond-breaking process rather than simultaneous bond rupture. It challenges thermal-activation-based models (e.g., Müller’s formula) that assume uniform charge states and image-charge potentials, showing instead that evaporation is governed by dynamic, anisotropic bond-breaking kinetics decoupled from sublimation energy.

title: Application of polymethacrylate from waste organic glass as a pour point depressor in heavy crude oil
research_summary: This work prepared polymethacrylate (PMA) via transesterification of waste polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA, organic glass) and aliphatic alcohols (hexadecanol or octadecanol), catalyzed by CaO, and evaluated its performance as a pour point depressant and viscosity reducer in heavy crude oil samples from Jinghe Oil Field. PMA-1 (from hexadecanol) achieved up to 7.1 °C pour point depression at 2000 ppm dosage and reduced viscosity by 63.7% at 50 °C; mechanism studies using DSC and polarized microscopy confirmed PMA-1 inhibits paraffin crystallization and modifies crystal morphology.

title: Investigation of isothermal continuous hot deformation behavior of the new as-cast alumina-forming austenitic alloy
research_summary: This study investigates the microstructural evolution of a new as-cast alumina-forming austenitic (AFA) heat-resistant alloy under multi-pass isothermal continuous hot deformation, focusing on grain evolution, recrystallization mechanisms (DRX and SRX), and the interaction between recrystallization and the segregated MC-type carbide phase.

title: Grain boundary-induced plasticity during thin film buckling
research_summary: The effect of grain boundaries (GB) on the buckling of an Al thin film delaminated from its substrate is investigated by means of molecular dynamics simulations at finite temperature. It is evidenced that the GB localizes the plasticity and deeply modifies the profile of the buckled thin film through the formation of a vertical fold at the location of the initial GB. Several plasticity mechanisms have been also described such as the development of extrinsic faults or the formation of uncommon C’D and CD’ dislocations. In this context, the folding angle and plastic strain in the film have been analyzed through a careful counting of the emerging dislocations at the film surfaces. The buckling profile of the film has been then analytically determined in the framework of the Föppl–von Karman’s (FvK) theory of thin plates and successfully compared with the simulated ones. The modifications of the film pattern in light of the different plastic (dislocations) and elastic (buckling) phenomena are finally discussed.

title: Exploring the expertise of large language models in materials science and metallurgical engineering
research_summary: This study evaluates 15 large language models (LLMs) on the MaScQA benchmark—a curated set of 644 questions from materials science and metallurgical engineering—to establish a baseline for their question-answering capabilities, identify top-performing models for future fine-tuning, and highlight domain-specific weaknesses (especially in numerical reasoning). The work supports an overarching project to fine-tune an LLM and integrate it into a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system for materials science applications.

title: Foundational Large Language Models for Materials Research
research_summary: This paper presents LLaMat, a family of domain-adapted large language models for materials science, developed through continued pretraining on materials literature and crystallographic data, followed by instruction- and task-finetuning. It demonstrates superior performance over commercial LLMs in materials-specific NLP, structured information extraction, and crystal structure generation, while revealing an 'adaptation rigidity' phenomenon where LLaMat-2 outperforms LLaMat-3 across diverse tasks.

title: Oxygen-mediated high uniform plasticity in α-β titanium alloys
research_summary: This paper presents a dual design strategy for α–β titanium alloys that transforms high oxygen from an embrittling liability into a performance enabler by (i) leveraging high oxygen (≥0.40%) to activate prominent pyramidal <c + a> slip in the α-phase, and (ii) engineering a tailored α–β microstructure through alloy design (Ti–O–Fe), laser-based powder bed fusion, and annealing to enable sustained slip transfer across α–β interfaces—achieving record uniform elongations (≥14% at yield strengths ≥980 MPa) while simultaneously resolving the yield strength–uniform elongation trade-off and oxygen embrittlement.

title: Fast firing of 3 mol% yttria-stabilized zirconia: On the effect of heating rate on sintering
file_name: 314_Journal of the American Cera‐stabilized zirconia  On the effect.pdf
research_summary: This paper investigates how heating rate affects the sintering behavior of ≈40 nm 3 mol% yttria-stabilized zirconia (3YSZ) powder, comparing fast firing (FF) with conventional sintering. Using dilatometry, density measurements, mercury porosimetry, SEM, and finite element modeling, the authors construct a master sintering curve (MSC) and evaluate densification pathways, pore evolution, closed pore formation, and microstructural development. They conclude that rapid heating yields only modest improvements (<2%–3% relative density) and that the MSC model remains valid, indicating the microstructure depends primarily on density—not thermal history.

title: Waste Loading and Durability of Calcium Aluminosilicate Glasses for Immobilization of Plutonium-Contaminated Material
file_name: 315_Int J of Appl Glass Sci - 2026 - Pam Aluminosilicate Glasses for.pdf
research_summary: Calcium aluminosilicate (CAS) glass was assessed for its ability to immobilize elements present in Plutonium-Contaminated Materials (PCM) including metals (Fe and Cr), polyvinyl chloride (PVC), and Pu (investigated using the nonradioactive surrogates Ce and Hf). Industrial-scale trial melts containing simulant inorganic and organic PCM were characterized to ascertain glass homogeneity, structure, and chemical durability. They were highly durable, comprising a glassy matrix with anorthite (CaAl2Si2O8) crystals. Redox conditions were such that 5–7 mol % Fe, from the melted steel drums, was incorporated in the glass phase, predominantly as Fe2+ in place of Ca, with no significant change to the glass structure. The solubility of Ce and Hf (as Pu surrogates), mixed metal, and PVC in CAS glass was investigated using a series of laboratory-scale melts and shown to exceed those measured in borosilicate glasses.

title: Design Principles of Optimizing Cementitious Glasses for the Disposal of Radioactive Waste
file_name: 317_Int J of Appl Glass Sci - 2026 - Tsekrekas s Glasses for the Disposal of.pdf
research_summary: We designed, synthesized, and characterized 26 cementitious calcium-magnesium aluminosilicate (CMAS) glasses using the chemical and mineralogical properties of ordinary Portland cement (OPC), ground, granulated blast furnace slag (BFS), and class F fly ash as bounding conditions. The compositions ranged from 31.3–43.8 mol% SiO2 , 2.8–14.3 mol% Al2 O3 , 32.1–52.1 mol% CaO, and 0.0–23.1 mol% MgO. The designed compositional space closely resembled that of reported BFS compositions. Our purpose for this design was to create glasses that would react with aqueous simulated low-level radioactive waste (LLW) solutions upon contact and form solid phases over time. The glasses’ structure was determined via Raman spectroscopy and was correlated with exothermic heat release measured by isothermal calorimetry. We observed a moderate to strong correlation between an increasing degree of depolymerization and increasing heat flow ( R2 = 0.66–0.78). After the completion of the isothermal calorimetry experiments, we examined the resulting solidified materials and observed no free-standing liquid—an important property for low-level waste disposition. Powder X-ray diffraction patterns collected on five representative solids, approximately 3 months after completion of the calorimetry experiments, contained reflections consistent with calcium-silicate hydrate and layered double hydroxide phases, supporting—though not conclusively demonstrating—that cementitious reactions occurred between the glasses and the simulated LLW.

title: Properties and Structures of MgO–CaO–Al2O3–SiO2 Glasses: Effects of Low-Iron Oxide and Redox
file_name: 318_Int J of Appl Glass Sci - 2026of MgO CaO Al2O3 SiO2 Glasses  Effects of Low‐Iron Oxide.pdf
research_summary: A series of mixed alkaline aluminosilicate glasses with low iron concentrations (0.04–0.64 wt% Fe2O3) was studied, covering a wide range of properties, including melt viscosity, liquidus temperature, simulated Rosseland mean radiative absorption/conduction, fiber tensile strength, water contact angle, and surface tension. To elucidate the local environments of ferric and ferrous ions in the glass network, multiple spectroscopic techniques (UV–vis–near infrared (NIR), fourier transform infrared (FTIR), and Raman spectroscopy) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were used.

title: Carbon Stoichiometry Regulation of High-Entropy Carbide–Silicon Carbide Composites for Enhanced Multifunctional Performance
file_name: 320_Journal of the American Ceramic Society - 2026 - Chen rbide Silicon.pdf
research_summary: Carbon stoichiometry regulation was employed to regulate the microstructure and properties of (Ti0.25 Ta0.25 Nb0.25 V0.25 )Cx ( x = 0.8, 1.0, and 1.2)-SiC high-entropy ceramic composites. Carbon-deficient and carbon-rich high-entropy carbide (HEC) powders were synthesized by a molten salt-assisted method and combined with 20 vol.% silicon carbide (SiC) for spark plasma sintering. The results demonstrate that carbon vacancies significantly enhance atomic diffusion and densification behavior. HEC0.8 -SiC exhibits the lowest sintering activation energy (572–578 kJ mol− 1 ) and achieves a high relative density of 99.82%. Benefiting from refined grains, high densification, and vacancy-induced lattice distortion, HEC0.8 -SiC delivers excellent mechanical properties with a hardness of 17.86 GPa, strength of 484.6 MPa, and fracture toughness of 4.6 MPa ⋅m1/2 . Moreover, optimized carbon vacancies promote the formation of protective V-rich oxide scales and enhance radiation tolerance by suppressing defect migration and accumulation. This work provides a vacancy-engineering strategy for designing multifunctional high-entropy ceramic composites for extreme environments.

title: Enhanced Magnetoelectric Coupling and Thermal Stability in Nd‐Doped BiFeO3 Ceramics Near the Morphotropic Phase Boundary
file_name: 322_Journal of the American Ceramic Society - 2026 -  in Nd‐Doped.pdf
research_summary: This study synthesizes Bi1-xNdxFeO3 ceramics to investigate how Nd doping drives a structural transition from polar R3c to antipolar Pbam phase, identifying a morphotropic phase boundary (MPB) near x = 0.16; it demonstrates significantly enhanced dynamic magnetoelectric coupling (~300 μV/(cm·Oe)) and exceptional thermal stability of the ME response up to 480 K at the MPB composition, attributing the enhancement to synergistic piezoelectricity and magnetostriction.

title: Synergistically Enhanced Piezoelectricity in W/Mn Co-Doped NBT Ceramics via Structural Distortion and Domain Regulation
file_name: 323_Journal of the Americazoelectricity in W Mn Co‐Doped NBT.pdf
research_summary: This study explores the effects of co-substitution with W and Mn at the B-site on the structural and functional properties of Na0.5Bi4.5Ti4O15 (NBT) ceramics, aiming to enhance piezoelectric performance for high-temperature applications. The optimal co-doped composition NBTWM5 achieves a piezoelectric coefficient (d33) of 34 pC/N — 100% higher than undoped NBT — while retaining a high Curie temperature (TC = 653°C) and elevated electrical resistivity (1.16 × 107 Ω·cm at 500°C). Enhancement is attributed to synergistic structural distortion and domain regulation induced by W/Mn doping.

title: Enhancing Dielectric Breakdown Strength of BiFeO3‐BaTiO3 Ceramics via Bi2 Ti2 O7 Doping
file_name: 324_Journal of the American of BiFeO3‐BaTiO3 Ceramics.pdf
research_summary: To develop high-performance capacitor materials, (1- x )(0.65BiFeO3 -0.35BaTiO3 )- x Bi2 Ti2 O7 ceramics (abbreviated as BFBT- x BTO, x = 0, 0.02, 0.04, 0.06, and 0.08) were synthesized by a solid-state reaction method. First, BFBT and BTO ceramic powders were prepared separately by the solid-state reaction method. Subsequently, these two powders were mixed homogeneously to fabricate BFBT- x BTO solid solution ceramics. x-Ray diffraction (XRD) analysis confirms that BTO diffuses into the crystal lattice of BFBT and forms a perovskite solid solution. SEM analysis reveals that the grain size of BFBT is reduced and the grain boundary density is increased after BTO doping, which facilitates the improvement of energy storage performance. Moreover, benefiting from the intrinsic advantages of BTO, such as low dielectric loss and low leakage current density, the breakdown strength ( Eb ) and the energy storage density of BFBT- x BTO ceramics are significantly enhanced. Meanwhile, the concentration of oxygen vacancies rises prominently in the outer grain regions, constructing a continuous protective barrier that also facilitates the enhancement of Eb . Among all compositions, the BFBT-0.02BTO ceramic exhibits optimal performance, featuring a high breakdown strength of 250 kV/cm, a high energy storage density of 4.14 J/cm3 , and excellent thermal stability.

title: Breaking the 3000◦C Melting Point Barrier in HfO2 : Molecular Dynamics Insights Into Doping and Non-Stoichiometry
file_name: 326_the 3000 C Melting Point Barrier in HfO2  Molecular Dynamics.pdf
research_summary: This work uses a machine learning potential (DP_SCAN) with SCAN functional accuracy to systematically investigate how cation doping and oxygen vacancy-mediated non-stoichiometry regulate the melting point of HfO2, predicting that optimized HfO1.85 achieves a melting point of 3042°C—exceeding the 3000°C barrier—and establishing a unified three-factor framework (synergistic bond strengthening, bond distribution uniformity, charge-compensating defect compatibility) to explain melting point regulation mechanisms.

title: Solid Solution in BaS–La2S3 Ceramics Produced by Mechanosynthesis and Their Potential for Rare-Earth Doping
file_name: 327_- Bayko - Solid Solution in BaS La2S3 Ceramics Produced by Mechanosynthesis.pdf
research_summary: This paper presents a low-temperature mechanosynthesis route to produce BaS–La2S3 ceramic powders, confirms the existence of a continuous solid solution between La2S3 and BaLa2S4, verifies adherence to Vegard’s law, identifies a sulfur-loss thermal event near 920 K, and demonstrates successful incorporation of up to 6 mol% Dy3+ without phase separation.

title: Effect of Steam Oxidation on Microstructure and Hoop Strength of Duplex SiCf /SiC Tube
file_name: 328_ Oxidation on Microstructure and Hoop Strength of.pdf
research_summary: This study investigates the temperature-dependent steam oxidation behavior and hoop strength degradation of silicon carbide fiber-reinforced silicon carbide (SiCf /SiC) tube exposed to steam at 600, 900, and 1200◦C for 10 days. Site-specific post-test characterization was combined with mechanical testing to establish the relationship between oxidation-induced damage and mechanical degradation.

title: Microstructural Evolution, Multi-Scale Strengthening and Mechanical Properties of TiC-Based Composites via Reactive Sintering
research_summary: This paper proposes a novel preparation method to synergistically enhance the sinterability and mechanical properties of TiC-based composites via in situ reaction among TiC, (Zr,Hf)C and Si. Based on this method, a multiphase microstructure is successfully constructed, consisting of nano-SiC particles, micro-scale Ti3SiC2, and (Ti,Zr,Hf)C solid solution within TiC matrix. Benefiting from this composite structure, the optimized composite achieves near-full densification (relative density > 99%) and exhibits superior mechanical properties, with a flexural strength of 972 MPa and a fracture toughness of 6.7 MPa ⋅m1/2. The enhancement in mechanical properties is attributed to a multi-scale synergistic strengthening mechanism, which includes solid solution strengthening at the atomic scale, grain boundary pinning by nano-SiC, coupled with crack deflection, and bridging induced by plate-like Ti3SiC2 grains.

title: Rapid fabrication of stretchable, ultratough, and rigid polymer materials
research_summary: This work reports a strategy for the rapid fabrication of stiff, tough, and stretchable polymers via photocuring copolymerization of acrylamide-based and hydroxyl-terminated acrylate monomers, enabling high-performance polymer materials with simultaneously high Young’s modulus (515.0 ± 100.9 MPa), yield strength (57.8 ± 1.8 MPa), toughness (135.7 ± 10.7 MJ/m3), and fracture strain (400.1 ± 46.1%), plus full strain recovery upon heating — all achieved within 1 minute using simple photopolymerization.

title: Exposure-Consistent Hydrogen Boundary Conditions Derived from Reactive Molecular Dynamics of Methane Decomposition on Nickel Surfaces
research_summary: This study uses ReaxFF-based reactive molecular dynamics to translate sustained CH4 and CH4 + H2O exposure on a Ni(211) surface under an accelerated closed-cell protocol at 1000–1350 K into exposure-conditioned hydrogen availability descriptors. It quantifies normalized Ni-associated H inventory, hydrogen partitioning between adsorbed and subsurface regions, and localization across CN-defined step and terrace regions to provide candidate inputs for downstream simulations of hydrogen transport, trapping, and degradation.

title: Ag Precursor-Assisted 350 °C Growth of Cu(In,Ga)Se2 Solar Cells Based on a Three-Stage Process
research_summary: This study investigates the use of an Ag precursor layer to enable low-temperature (350 °C) growth of Cu(In,Ga)Se2 (CIGS) solar cell absorbers using the conventional three-stage deposition process, targeting bifacial and tandem photovoltaic applications. The authors first optimize Ag precursor thickness (5, 10, 25 nm) at a high-temperature reference condition (600 °C), balancing improved film quality against reduced net acceptor density. They identify 10 nm as optimal and then transfer this condition to low-temperature deposition (350 °C). Characterization shows Ag incorporation improves minority-carrier lifetime, diode parameters, and Urbach energy at 350 °C, enabling ACIGS solar cells to maintain ~15% power conversion efficiency, whereas non-Ag CIGS devices degrade severely.

title: Band Gap Narrowing in Oxychlorosulfide Photocatalysts through Aliovalent Cl-to-S Anion Substitution
research_summary: This study demonstrates aliovalent Cl-to-S substitution in the oxychlorosulfide La5Ti6O15S3Cl3 by simultaneously replacing Cl– with S2– and Ti4+ with Ta5+, which elevates the valence-band maximum via increased S 3p orbital contribution, narrows the band gap, and yields visible-light-responsive H2-evolution photocatalysts.
